Techniques Used: Genome size and GC content estimation
Data & Platforms: Oak Ridge Integrated Field Research Challenge (OR-IFRC)
Kessler Atmospheric and Ecological Field Station
Application Areas: Soil Carbon Dynamics and Climate Feedbacks
Nitrogen Cycle Regulation in Oligotrophic Environments
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Metabolic Niche Partitioning via Isotope-Tracing: Utilizing 15N stable isotope labeling coupled with kinetic analysis to resolve substrate preferences (e.g., ammonia vs. urea) and regulatory strategies among distinct ammonia-oxidizing lineages (AOA, comammox, AOB), explaining their coexistence through minimized direct competition.

Quorum Sensing-Driven Metabolic Coordination: Integrating metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data from global ocean surveys (e.g., Tara Oceans) to identify quorum sensing systems (AI-2, DSF) in marine AOA, demonstrating how cell-density signaling orchestrates nitrogen/carbon metabolism and cross-kingdom metabolite exchange.

Phylogenomic Discovery of Novel Lineages: Employing comparative genomics of Metagenome-Assembled Genomes (MAGs) and Single-Amplified Genomes (SAGs) to characterize novel taxa like 'Candidatus' Nitrosomirales, revealing horizontal gene transfer events that expand known metabolic capabilities (e.g., formate oxidation) in undersampled environments.

Process-Based Ecosystem Modeling Integration: Linking experimental warming impacts on microbial functional traits (cellulose decomposition) to the Microbial-ENzyme Decomposition (MEND) model, thereby reducing parameter uncertainty and improving predictive accuracy of soil carbon dynamics under climate change scenarios.
Summary Description: Wei Qin is a microbial ecologist specializing in the biogeochemical roles of ammonia-oxidizing microorganisms across marine, terrestrial, and subsurface ecosystems. By integrating stable isotope tracing, high-throughput transcriptomics, and phylogenomic reconstruction of MAGs/SAGs, Qin elucidates the metabolic strategies, quorum sensing mechanisms, and evolutionary history of key nitrifiers. A central focus is resolving nitrogen cycle imbalances in oligotrophic oceans and understanding how microbial community shifts drive soil carbon decomposition under climate warming. Qin’s work bridges molecular microbial ecology with ecosystem modeling (MEND), providing mechanistic insights into global nutrient cycling and carbon feedbacks.
